props.gloss_en: the mishna: from a private domain to a private domain with the public domain between -- R' Akiva holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
side 1: they dispute below ten handbreadths, over whether an object in the airspace counts as set down; above ten all agree he is exempt, and we do not derive throwing from passing
side 2: they dispute above ten, over whether throwing is derived from passing; below ten all agree he is liable, for an object in the airspace counts as set down
the baraita: from a private domain to a private domain, passing through the public domain itself -- R' Akiva holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
since it says 'the public domain itself', plainly they dispute below ten handbreadths
(candidate) the baraita speaks of passing an object by hand
(survivor) the baraita speaks of throwing
R' Elazar: one who carries out a load above ten handbreadths is liable, for such was the carrying of the sons of Kehat
R' Elazar: R' Akiva holds him liable even [where it passed] above ten handbreadths
R' Elazar: what the baraita teaches, 'the public domain itself', is to let you know the strength of the Rabbis' position
Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi: within three handbreadths [of the ground] -- all agree he is liable
above ten handbreadths -- all agree he is exempt
from three up to ten -- we have come to the dispute of R' Akiva and the Rabbis
the baraita: within three -- all agree he is liable
above ten -- it is only [forbidden] on account of shvut
and if the domains were his own -- it is permitted
from three to ten -- R' Akiva holds him liable and the Sages exempt
Rav: two houses on two sides of the public domain -- it is forbidden to throw from one to the other
Shmuel: it is permitted to throw from one to the other
we established Rav's ruling where one house is high and one low -- sometimes [the object] falls and he comes to fetch it
anything less than three [handbreadths apart] is as if joined (lavud)
[the source of lavud is] that the public domain cannot be levelled with plane and scraper
the sukka mishna: one who lets the walls down from above -- if they are three handbreadths above the ground, [the sukka] is invalid (by inference: less than three, valid)
there the reason is that it is a partition through which goats pass
rather, 'anything less than three is as if joined' -- it is a received halakha
the baraita: from the public domain to the public domain with a private domain between -- Rabbi holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
Rav and Shmuel: Rabbi held him liable only for a roofed private domain, for we say a house is as if full; an unroofed one, not
Rabbi would obligate him two [sin-offerings]: one for carrying out and one for carrying in
Rabbi: 'things', 'the things', 'these are the things' (Ex 35:1) -- these are the thirty-nine labours stated to Moses at Sinai
the baraita: [one threw] from a private domain to the public domain and it passed four cubits in the public domain -- R' Yehuda holds him liable
...and the Sages exempt him
Rav Yehuda in Shmuel's name: R' Yehuda would obligate him two -- one for carrying out and one for passing [four cubits]
R' Yehuda obligates only one, and the Sages exempt entirely
where he said: as soon as it goes out into the public domain, let it rest
R' Yehuda holds: we say an object in the airspace counts as set down, so his intention was realised
the Rabbis hold: we do not say it counts as set down, so his intention was not realised
but for a tolada [done] in the place of an av R' Yehuda does not obligate
R' Yehuda adds the shovet [to the primary labours]
...and the medakdek
they said to him: the shovet is included in meisech
the medakdek is included in oreg
[the baraita is where] he did each alone; they dispute whether these are avot (R' Yehuda) or tolados (the Rabbis)
Rav Ashi: where he says 'wherever it wishes, let it rest'
